rationale: n-body is a tiny program dominated by a single hot numeric loop with heavy floating-point arithmetic and simple, predictable control flow, so the weight table favors cheap, arithmetic- and structure-hiding passes over expensive control-flow transforms. SUB gets the strongest security/diversity weights because the loop's arithmetic ops are its core logic and substitutions cost little even in a hot loop; SPLIT and IGV are cheap diversifiers that complicate basic-block layout and interprocedural structure without measurable loop overhead; ICALL and IBR get moderate weights since a handful of indirected calls/branches raises reverse-engineering effort at acceptable cost. BCF is heavily discounted (high runtime/size weights mean the compiler should shy away) because opaque predicates add per-iteration overhead in the hot loop while being well-known and easily stripped, and FLA is similarly down-weighted since the benchmark's trivial control flow offers little to flatten and the dispatcher loop would tax every iteration; both remain listed at low appeal rather than omitted in case per-function features (e.g., cold wrappers) make limited application profitable. All passes carry low CorrectnessRisk weights except FLA/IBR/IGV, whose transformations of control flow and linkage warrant slightly more caution to preserve numeric output fidelity.
